title: Kawasaki disease: greatest risk is coronary artery aneurysm
vignette: A 4-year-old boy is brought to the clinic by his parents for evaluation of fever that has lasted 5 days. He has been more irritable than usual and has had 3 episodes of vomiting. The patient has no prior medical conditions. He traveled internationally this year to visit his grandparents and cousins. Immunizations are up to date. Temperature is 38.9 C (102 F). Physical examination shows bilateral conjunctival injection with no exudates. The tongue is bright red and the lips are cracked. Nonpitting edema is present on the hands and feet, and there is a maculopapular rash on the arms and legs. Which of the following complications is this patient at greatest risk for developing?

clues.note: Fever for at least 5 days is a required criterion for Kawasaki disease (plus 4 of the mucocutaneous findings).

clues.text: bilateral conjunctival injection with no exudates
clues.note: Bilateral NON-exudative conjunctivitis is a diagnostic feature of Kawasaki disease.

clues.text: tongue is bright red and the lips are cracked
clues.note: Mucositis - 'strawberry tongue' and cracked/fissured red lips - is a hallmark of Kawasaki disease.

clues.text: Nonpitting edema is present on the hands and feet
clues.note: Extremity changes (edema/erythema of hands and feet, later desquamation) are a Kawasaki criterion.

clues.text: maculopapular rash on the arms and legs
clues.note: A polymorphous rash is another Kawasaki criterion; together these features point to the vasculitis and its cardiac risk.

whatMatters: Fever >=5 days + bilateral nonexudative conjunctivitis + mucositis (strawberry tongue/cracked lips) + hand/foot edema + polymorphous rash = KAWASAKI DISEASE (medium-vessel vasculitis of young children). Its most serious complication is CORONARY ARTERY ANEURYSM. Answer B. Timely IVIG (within 10 days) reduces this risk.
strategy: Recognize Kawasaki (fever >=5 days + 4 of: conjunctivitis, mucositis, extremity changes, rash, cervical lymphadenopathy), then recall it attacks MEDIUM arteries - especially the coronaries -> coronary artery aneurysm (risk of thrombosis/MI). Reject aortic dissection (large-vessel/Marfan/HTN), encephalitis (measles - but this is Kawasaki), glomerulonephritis (post-strep), pulmonary cavitation (TB), and splenic rupture (mono).

eliminations.label: Aortic dissection - large-vessel (HTN/Marfan)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a tear in the aortic wall, associated with long-standing hypertension or connective-tissue disease (Marfan). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: Kawasaki affects MEDIUM arteries (coronaries), not the aorta; large-vessel inflammation is not a feature. ✅ Correct if: hypertensive/Marfan aortic pathology.

eliminations.label: Encephalitis - measles complication (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: brain inflammation, a complication of measles (which can also have fever + conjunctivitis + rash). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: measles rash starts on the face with Koplik spots/cough/coryza; this child has strawberry tongue, hand/foot edema, and cracked lips = Kawasaki, whose danger is cardiac. ✅ Correct if: measles (with Koplik spots and cephalocaudal rash).

eliminations.label: Proliferative glomerulonephritis - post-streptococcal
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: immune-complex GN after group A strep. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it follows strep pharyngitis/impetigo (with a different rash pattern) and is not a Kawasaki complication. ✅ Correct if: post-streptococcal GN (hematuria, edema, ↑ASO).

eliminations.label: Pulmonary cavitation - tuberculosis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: lung cavities from reactivation TB. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: although the child traveled, the mucocutaneous findings define Kawasaki, not TB. ✅ Correct if: chronic cough/weight loss with apical cavitary lung disease.

eliminations.label: Splenic rupture - infectious mononucleosis
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a complication of EBV mononucleosis (splenomegaly). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: mono features prominent cervical/generalized lymphadenopathy and pharyngitis, not strawberry tongue + hand/foot edema. ✅ Correct if: EBV mono with splenomegaly (avoid contact sports).

reasoning: Fever >=5 days + conjunctivitis + mucositis + extremity edema + polymorphous rash = Kawasaki disease
Kawasaki is a vasculitis of MEDIUM-sized arteries in young children
It preferentially inflames the coronary arteries -> coronary artery aneurysm
mechanism: Kawasaki disease is a vasculitis of MEDIUM-sized arteries affecting young children (usually <5 years). Diagnosis requires FEVER for at least 5 days PLUS at least 4 of: bilateral nonexudative conjunctivitis, mucositis (fissured red lips, strawberry tongue), extremity changes (edema/erythema of hands and feet, later periungual desquamation), a polymorphous rash, and cervical lymphadenopathy (>1.5 cm). The most serious complication is inflammation of the CORONARY ARTERIES, producing CORONARY ARTERY ANEURYSMS; these can thrombose, calcify, or rupture, causing myocardial ischemia/infarction or sudden death, and are the leading cause of morbidity. Although the acute illness is self-limited, prompt treatment with intravenous immunoglobulin (plus aspirin) within 10 days of symptom onset markedly reduces the incidence of coronary aneurysms. The distractors are complications of other diseases: aortic dissection (hypertension/Marfan), encephalitis (measles), post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, pulmonary cavitation (TB), and splenic rupture (mononucleosis).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Rheum/Peds > Kawasaki disease: medium-vessel vasculitis; fever >=5 days + conjunctivitis, mucositis (strawberry tongue), extremity changes, rash, cervical lymphadenopathy; coronary artery aneurysm; treat IVIG + aspirin.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: The mucocutaneous criteria define Kawasaki; its 'greatest risk' complication is coronary aneurysm.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on Kawasaki criteria, strawberry tongue, mucositis, medium-vessel vasculitis, or coronary aneurysm? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Encephalitis = measles; aortic dissection = HTN/Marfan; GN = post-strep; cavitation = TB; splenic rupture = mono - not Kawasaki.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: Kawasaki -> coronary artery aneurysm; IVIG + aspirin within 10 days reduces risk.

keywords.front: Fever >=5 days + conjunctivitis + strawberry tongue + hand/foot edema + rash

firstAid.detail: Rheum: medium-vessel vasculitis; coronary artery aneurysm is the key complication.
Peds > encephalitis (measles), GN (post-strep), cavitation (TB), splenic rupture (mono).
Peds > IVIG + aspirin within 10 days to prevent aneurysms.

memoryHook: Kawasaki = a feverish toddler with a strawberry tongue, red eyes, and swollen hands whose real danger is hidden in the heart: coronary artery aneurysms.
